report: Facilitation complete (15 turns). All three sisters' concerns were collected as noncontroversial essences and confirmed by each person: C — her share not reduced by anyone's special deal, while B still gets real help; A — a real chance to buy the house at a manageable price with no one pressured, a discount explorable only with C's genuine agreement; B — enough for a real start on a dance studio (amount TBD) plus time to think. I added my own concern (a plan all can live with and that's feasible, e.g. house price covering B's needs). Draft options were shared: market-value sale to A, third-party sale, or a discounted sale only if C freely agrees after an independent appraisal. Unresolved items, recorded as such: whether any discount can meet C's fairness concern; whether a one-third share suffices for B's studio; and the will's actual division of shares, which needs a lawyer. Agreed next steps: B works out studio costs, C and A treat an independent appraisal as a shared factual starting point (not agreement), the will is reviewed legally, and no decisions are rushed. Nothing was settled or signed off; C explicitly noted the appraisal is not consent to a discounted sale.
